title: Spreading a local alteration diagram with its proper covering witness
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative Noetherian integral domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be prime, and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}B_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Fix finitely many nonempty integral Noetherian schemes $T_i$ [def-pc-integral-scheme] with dominant generically finite finite-type maps $f_i:T_i\to S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose given an integral Noetherian scheme $P$, a proper surjective generically finite map $g:P\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-surjective-morphism], a finite open cover $P=\bigcup_iP_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and $S$-morphisms $h_i:P_i\to T_i$. Here dominant means dense image and generically finite means a finite extension of function fields, with function field the local ring at the generic point. Then there is $a\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ and a diagram over $S_a=\operatorname{Spec}B[1/a]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] consisting of integral Noetherian schemes $T_{a,i},P_a$, dominant generically finite finite-type maps $f_{a,i}:T_{a,i}\to S_a$, a proper surjective generically finite map $g_a:P_a\to S_a$, a finite open cover $P_a=\bigcup_iP_{a,i}$ and $S_a$-morphisms $h_{a,i}:P_{a,i}\to T_{a,i}$. Its base change along $S\to S_a$ is isomorphic to the entire specified diagram, including the indexed open cover and all its morphisms [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every $b\notin\mathfrak q$ with $D(b)\subseteq D(a)$, restriction to $D(b)$ retains all these properties and still recovers the specified diagram over $S$. No regularity or excellence assumption is made. Here Noetherian for a scheme means quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth].

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Lemma 4.4, first proof paragraph, printed p.5: spreading the alteration cover and its proper witness from B_q to B[1/a]. Properness ingredient: Stacks limits.tex, Tag 081F, lemma-eventually-proper. The full diagram statement includes integrality/generic finiteness and open-cover data, not just properness. Archival copy WANTED; finite-presentation and surjectivity ingredients identified in report.md.

proof.text: Index the principal neighbourhoods by $c\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$, ordered by divisibility. They are directed, since $c,d$ both divide $cd$, and $B_{\mathfrak q}=\varinjlim_cB[1/c]$; the affine-limit lemma gives $S=\varprojlim_cS_c$ with affine transitions and affine qcqs stages. All these rings are Noetherian by localization. Each $P_i$ is Noetherian by open-subscheme permanence. Its inclusion into $P$ is quasi-compact by the locally Noetherian open-immersion lemma and hence finite type; finite-type composition makes $P_i\to S$ finite type. Thus all vertices are quasi-compact Noetherian schemes. The locally Noetherian quasi-separatedness lemma and morphism permanence make these structure maps quasi-separated. The locally finite type to finite presentation lemma therefore makes them finitely presented. Here properness includes finite type. Thus the object-descent hypotheses hold for every vertex, including each indexed open-cover vertex.

source.place: Tags 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective), 081F (lemma-eventually-proper); explicit assembly of the spreading paragraph of Kurano–Shimomoto Lemma 4.4, printed p.5.

proof.text: Apply object descent to the finitely many vertices $T_i,P,P_i$, choosing a common stage $S_c$. Apply finite-diagram lifting to their given structure arrows, inclusions $P_i\to P$, and maps $h_i$; include the finitely many relations $f_i h_i=g|_{P_i}$. We obtain a finite-presentation diagram over $S_c$ and a natural isomorphism from its pullback to the entire specified diagram. This retains the chosen $h_i$, rather than replacing them with arbitrary maps. Its sources are Noetherian by finite type over the Noetherian affine base. Every diagram arrow is locally finite type: its composite with the structure map is locally finite type; hence it is locally finitely presented over its locally Noetherian target.

source.place: Tags 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective), 081F (lemma-eventually-proper); explicit assembly of the spreading paragraph of Kurano–Shimomoto Lemma 4.4, printed p.5.

proof.text: For each descended inclusion use open-immersion descent, and enlarge the common stage so all are open immersions. Apply finite-family joint-surjectivity descent to the maps $P_{c,i}\to P_c$, obtaining a genuine indexed open cover. Apply properness descent to $P_c\to S_c$, and surjectivity descent to the same map. All relevant sources, targets and bases are qcqs, all arrows in question are locally finitely presented, and the limit arrows have precisely the required properties. There are finitely many stage requirements, so choose a common multiple of their indices outside $\mathfrak q$; the open, cover, proper and surjective properties persist under the intervening base changes.

source.place: Tags 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective), 081F (lemma-eventually-proper); explicit assembly of the spreading paragraph of Kurano–Shimomoto Lemma 4.4, printed p.5.

proof.text: Apply integrality near a prime to each $T_{c,i}$ and $P_c$ over $B[1/c]$ at $\mathfrak qB[1/c]$, since its prime localization is the specified integral scheme. Clear the finitely many denominators of the resulting elements and multiply them with $c$ to obtain $a\notin\mathfrak q$. To check dominance and generic finiteness, let $X_a$ be any one of these integral models. On a nonempty affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ meeting $X_{\mathfrak q}$ the localization $C\to (B\setminus\mathfrak q)^{-1}C$ has nonzero domain target. Since $C$ is a domain it is injective and its zero prime contracts to zero; hence the generic point of $X_{\mathfrak q}$ maps to the generic point of $X_a$. The base generic point likewise identifies through $B[1/a]\to B_{\mathfrak q}$. The affine fraction-field description identifies both function fields with the original ones, compatibly with their field embedding. Thus all $f_{a,i}$ and $g_a$ are dominant generically finite. Finite type and Noetherianity persist after this shrinking.

source.place: Tags 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), 0EUU (lemma-descend-open-immersion), 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective), 081F (lemma-eventually-proper); explicit assembly of the spreading paragraph of Kurano–Shimomoto Lemma 4.4, printed p.5.

proof.text: Finally let $b\notin\mathfrak q$ with $D(b)\subseteq D(a)$. Base change the chosen diagram to $D(b)$. The indexed open cover remains a cover by inverse images, properness persists, and the image formula preserves surjectivity. Finite type persists and the sources are Noetherian. Each restricted $T_{a,i}$ and $P_a$ is an open subscheme of an integral scheme containing its generic point: dominance puts that point over $(0)\in D(b)$. It is therefore nonempty integral, with the same function field, by localization of its affine domain charts. The fraction-field description consequently preserves generic finiteness and dominance. Associativity of fibre products identifies its pullback to $S$ with the original specified diagram, with the same cover and all the same arrows.
